sources.entry: Agent Teams AI - Desktop control center for coordinating autonomous AI coding agent teams across multiple providers.

summary.one_liner: A free, open-source Electron desktop app for coordinating teams of autonomous AI coding agents across multiple providers, with a kanban board, live task logs, and per-action approvals.
summary.what_it_does: Lets you assemble a team of AI agents from a single prompt, each with its own role, and watch them work in parallel while tasks move across a kanban board. Agents message each other, create and comment on tasks, and review each other's work, and you can DM any agent or comment on a task. It supports a free model with no sign-in, plus auto-detected Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode runtimes and connectable providers such as Cursor, SuperGrok, GitHub Copilot, Z.AI, MiniMax, and Kiro. The app also provides token and cost analytics with budget alerts, a per-task log view, an integrated terminal and code editor with Git support, diff review with accept/reject per hunk, and optional git worktree isolation per teammate. An MCP server folder is included for connecting external tools.
use_cases: coordinate multiple AI coding agents on a project
run autonomous agent teams with a kanban board
review AI-generated code changes before applying them
track token usage and cost of AI coding sessions
use a free AI coding model without signing up
run parallel agents in separate git worktrees
notable: Starts with a free model that needs no account, API key, or card, and can also use Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor and other providers
Kanban board where agents create, comment on, and move tasks, with a per-task log and message view
Per-action approval mode for supported tool calls, or fully autonomous operation
Token analytics with monthly token or cost budgets and alerts at 80% and 100%
Includes a Terminal Platform SDK vendored under vendor/terminal-platform and 29 interface languages
caveats: Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run; the README says to choose 'More info' then 'Run anyway'
Source builds need Node.js 26.11.1 or 24.16.0 LTS and pnpm 11.22.0; on macOS, Node 24 requires macOS 13.5+
The standalone HTTP dashboard has no built-in authentication and is meant only for local or trusted-network use
Some Linux RDP sessions need the AGENT_TEAMS_DISABLE_GPU=1 workaround; the web version is still in active development
